title: Wilds of Selection
subject: Science: How Natural Selection Works
intro: The three steps, asexual vs sexual reproduction, mutations, and the key takeaways (populations, generations, the hawk and the mice). Miss one and it comes back in new words, or broken into smaller steps.

questions.q: Step 1 of natural selection: ______ exists in a population.
questions.explain: First there must be variation: the members of a population are different from each other (colour, size, speed...).

variants.q: Some mice are black and some are tan. Which step of natural selection is this?
choices: Step 1: variation exists in the population
Step 3: the trait becomes more common
It is not part of natural selection

variants.q: Before nature can 'select' anything, the organisms in a population must be ______ from each other.

steps.q: 'Variation' means the members of a group are...
Natural selection needs something to choose between. So step 1 is: ______ exists.

questions.q: Step 2: organisms with helpful adaptations ______ better and ______ more than those without them.
questions.explain: Helpful traits (like camouflage) help an organism stay alive AND have more babies than the others.
questions.review: Step 2: helpful traits survive and reproduce more

variants.q: On dark rocks, black mice are eaten less by hawks than tan mice. Which step of natural selection is this?
choices: Step 2: helpful traits survive and reproduce more
Step 3: the trait becomes common in the population

variants.q: Step 2 needs TWO things to happen for the organisms with helpful traits. Which pair?
choices: They survive better and reproduce more
They learn faster and teach others

steps.q: An 'adaptation' is a trait that...
choices: helps an organism survive in its environment

steps.q: Why does surviving longer matter for natural selection?
choices: Survivors live long enough to have offspring
Survivors become a new species right away

questions.q: Step 3: over generations, these beneficial traits become more common in the ______.
questions.explain: Because helpful-trait organisms have more babies, the trait spreads through the whole population over the generations.
questions.review: Step 3: trait becomes more common in the population

variants.q: After many generations on dark rocks, most of the mice are black. Which step is this?
choices: Step 3: the trait became more common in the population

variants.q: Put the steps in order: (A) the helpful trait becomes common, (B) variation exists, (C) helpful traits survive and reproduce more.

steps.q: A 'population' is...
choices: all the organisms of one kind living in one area

steps.q: If black mice have more babies every generation, black mice become more ______.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of natural selection?
choices: Variation exists → helpful traits survive and reproduce more → the trait becomes common
The trait becomes common → variation exists → helpful traits survive
Organisms decide to change → they pass it on → variation exists
Helpful traits survive → variation exists → the trait disappears
questions.explain: Variation comes first, then survival and reproduction, then the trait spreads over generations.

variants.q: Rabbits: (1) most rabbits are now white, (2) some rabbits are white and some brown, (3) white rabbits hide in snow and survive more. Correct order?

questions.q: ______ reproduction: offspring are genetically identical to the parent. NO variation.
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction uses one parent, so the offspring are copies (clones) with no variation.

variants.q: A bacterium splits into two copies of itself. What kind of reproduction is this?
Which kind of reproduction makes offspring with NO variation?

steps.q: How many parents are needed in ASEXUAL reproduction?
'Genetically identical' means the offspring...
choices: have the exact same DNA as the parent

questions.q: ______ reproduction: offspring HAVE variation from each other and their parents.
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, so every offspring is a bit different.

variants.q: Two cats have a litter of kittens. Every kitten looks a little different. What kind of reproduction made this happen?
Why do brothers and sisters look different from each other?
choices: Sexual reproduction mixes their parents' genes differently each time
They ate different food as babies

steps.q: How many parents are needed in SEXUAL reproduction?

questions.q: Sexual reproduction results in a ______ of the parents' genes.
questions.explain: Each offspring gets a mix of genes from mom and dad, so offspring differ from the parents AND from their siblings.

variants.q: A puppy gets some genes from its mother and some from its father. This is called a ______ of the parents' genes.

steps.q: Where do a baby's genes come from in sexual reproduction?

questions.q: Evolution through natural selection happens much ______ in populations that reproduce sexually.
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction makes more variation, and variation is what natural selection works on, so change happens faster.

variants.q: Fish A reproduces sexually. Fish B makes clones of itself. The lake gets warmer. Which can adapt faster?
choices: Fish A, because its babies have more variation
Fish B, because clones are stronger

variants.q: True or false: evolution happens SLOWER in organisms that reproduce sexually.

steps.q: Which makes MORE variation?
More variation gives natural selection more to choose from. So change happens...

questions.q: It is faster in sexual reproducers due to ______ genetic diversity.
questions.explain: Mixing genes gives a population higher genetic diversity, so there are more traits for nature to select from.

variants.q: A population that reproduces sexually has ______ genetic diversity than one that makes clones.

steps.q: 'Genetic diversity' means...
choices: how different the genes in a population are

questions.q: Mutation: ______ in DNA when it replicates (copies itself).
questions.explain: A mutation is a mistake made when DNA copies itself. It can create a trait not found in either parent.
questions.review: Mutation = a mistake in copied DNA

variants.q: A bacterium copies its DNA and makes a small mistake. Now it has a brand-new trait. This is a ______.
A kitten has a coat colour that NEITHER parent has. What most likely caused it?

steps.q: When does DNA 'replicate'?
A mistake while copying DNA is called a...

questions.q: A mutation can result in different traits that are...
questions.explain: Because the DNA changed, the offspring can have a trait neither parent had.

variants.q: Mutations matter for natural selection because they...

questions.q: Natural selection leads to changes in ______ over time, NOT individuals.
questions.explain: One tan mouse can't turn black. The POPULATION changes because more black mice survive and have babies.

variants.q: Over 100 years, a moth population changes from mostly light to mostly dark. What changed?
choices: The population: more dark moths each generation
The moths chose to be dark

variants.q: Can one tan mouse turn black during its life because of hawks?
choices: No: individuals don't change; the population does

steps.q: An 'individual' is...
Natural selection changes the whole ______, not one animal.

questions.q: Traits that help organisms survive and reproduce become more ______.
questions.explain: Helpful traits get passed on more often, so over time more of the population has them.

variants.q: Finches with thick beaks crack the only seeds left after a drought. In later generations, thick beaks become...

steps.q: Organisms with a helpful trait have MORE babies. Their babies often...

questions.explain: Natural selection is slow. You see the change only after many generations of parents and offspring.

variants.q: How long does it take for most of a mouse population to become black?
Why do bacteria evolve resistance in months, but elephants take thousands of years?
choices: Bacteria go through generations much faster
Elephants are too big to change

steps.q: A 'generation' is...
choices: one step from parents to their offspring

questions.q: Mice move to an area with very dark rocks. Some mice are black, some tan. Which mice do the hawks spot more easily?
questions.scene: A hawk circles over the dark rocks of a new valley where {h} watches a family of mice.
questions.win: {h} spots it too. The hawk swoops on the easy target and {h} records the result.
questions.lose: The hawk screeches and dives at {h} instead!
questions.explain: Tan stands out against dark rocks, so hawks see and eat tan mice more often.

variants.q: A white rabbit and a brown rabbit live in a snowy forest. Which will owls see more easily?

questions.q: Because tan mice are eaten more, what does the next generation of mice look like?
choices: A higher fraction of black mice than before
A higher fraction of tan mice
questions.scene: Seasons pass in the dark valley. {h} returns to count the mice.
questions.explain: Black mice survive to reproductive age more often and leave more offspring, so the next generation has more black mice.

variants.q: Beetles on brown bark come in red, blue and brown. Birds eat the bright ones. After many generations most beetles will be...

steps.q: Which mice survive long enough to have babies?
Black parents mostly have ______ babies.

questions.q: In the mice story, which part shows Step 1 (variation)?
choices: Due to genetic variation, some mice are black and others tan
Hawks eat tan mice more often
The next generation has more black mice
The mice moved to a new area
questions.explain: Variation means differences already in the population: some black, some tan. That is step 1.

variants.q: In the mice story, which part shows Step 2 (helpful traits survive and reproduce more)?
choices: Black mice are eaten less and leave more offspring
Some mice are black and some tan
The mice moved to dark rocks

variants.q: In the mice story, which part shows Step 3 (the trait becomes common)?
choices: Each generation has a higher fraction of black mice

questions.q: Giraffes have long necks. Which explanation fits natural selection?
choices: Giraffes born with longer necks reached more food, survived and had more babies
Each giraffe stretched its neck and passed the stretch on
Giraffes decided they wanted long necks
Long necks appeared all at once in one generation
questions.explain: Natural selection works on traits organisms are BORN with. Stretching during life is not passed on in DNA.

variants.q: A dog learns to open doors. Will her puppies be born knowing how?
choices: No: learned skills are not in the DNA
Yes, if she teaches them before birth
